question_text: Provide a breakdown of your community-wide emissions by sector.
col5_Comment:
This figure represents total transportation emissions which combines on-road, transit, off-road, waterborne, and rail transportation emissions.
Two different datasets were used:

2) The Origin-Destination model with VMT that represents 100% of all in-boundary transportation and 50% cross-boundary transportation.

4.3.3 Agricultura, Silvicultura y otros Usos del Suelo (AFOLU)
El sector de Agricultura, silvicultura y otros usos del suelo (Agriculture, forestry, and other land use, AFOLU, por sus siglas en inglés) produce emisiones de GEI a través de una variedad de vías, incluidos los cambios de usos del suelo que alteran la composición del suelo, el metano producido en los procesos digestivos de los animales de granja, y el manejo de nutrientes para fines agrícolas (WRI 2014). Sin embargo, el presente estudio incluye las emisiones directas de GEI por el cambio de uso del suelo, especialmente el cambio de tierras forestales a tierras agrícolas y las emisiones derivadas por la aplicación de fertilizantes nitrogenados para los cultivos anuales. En el caso de los cultivos como caña de azúcar, banano, palma aceitera y café se incluyen las emisiones que se reportan en la huella de carbono para cada cultivo. Las emisiones por la tenencia de ganado vacuno y de granja, no se incluyó en la estimación por la falta de información a nivel municipal y del Ministerio de Agricultura Ganadería y Alimentación -MAGA-.
4.3.3.1 Cambio de uso del suelo
El cambio de uso del suelo y en particular el cambio de tierras forestales a tierras agrícolas, contribuyen a la emisión de una importante cantidad de GEI, ya que los bosques son sumideros que almacenan carbono en los árboles, en la materia orgánica caída y en el suelo, por lo que la pérdida de bosque o su degradación implica que el carbono retenido se libera a

De acuerdo a Hewson et al (2014), menciona que para realizar este cálculo, se necesita conocer los datos de actividad y el factor de emisión, tal como se ha realizado en las fuentes de emisión antes reportadas. Desechos Sólidos Municipales -DSM-
De acuerdo a WRI (2014), las ciudades/municipios producen desechos sólidos y aguas residuales (denominados en conjunto “desechos/residuos”) que pueden ser dispuestos y/o tratados en las instalaciones dentro de los límites de la ciudad, o transportados a otras ciudades para su tratamiento. La disposición y el tratamiento de residuos producen emisiones de GEI a través de la descomposición aeróbica o anaeróbica, o la incineración.
Para fines de este estudio, se tomaron en cuenta las emisiones de CH4 procedente de los desechos que no se incineran/queman y que se degradan bajo condiciones aeróbicas, y se contabilizaron las emisiones de CO2 producto de la incineración/quema de los desechos a cielo abierto. Para realizar el cálculo, se llevaron a cabo los siguientes pasos: primero, se determinó la generación de desechos per cápita para Guatemala, el cual corresponde a 0.45 Kg/habitante/día para el área urbana y 0.33 Kg/habitante/día para el área rural, según datos publicados por IARNA-URL 2012. Posteriormente se calculó la cantidad de desechos sólidos generados en el 2017 para todo el municipio, en función a los datos de población y la generación de desechos per cápita, donde además, se calculó la fracción de los desechos que se queman y la otra fracción que no se quema y se degradan bajo condiciones aeróbicas. Este indicador, se obtuvo de la información publicada por INE (2015), donde mencionan que en Guatemala, el 44% de la población (11.90% área urbana y 32.10% área rural), quema sus desechos sólidos. El resto son llevados a zonas reguladas como los vertederos municipales o a zonas no reguladas (clandestinas) donde se deposita y que son fuente de emisión de GEI.

Sumbawa Regency, as an agropolitan region with a high dependence on the agriculture, livestock, and fisheries sectors, experiences real impacts of climate change such as crop failures and decreased seaweed production. On the other hand, the transportation sector is a major contributor to GHG emissions, mainly due to the combustion of fossil fuels by motorized vehicles. Sumbawa Regency shows a high level of fuel consumption, making it one of the largest contributors to GHG emissions in West Nusa Tenggara Province. This study aims to calculate the contribution of the transportation sector to total GHG emissions in Sumbawa Regency, as a basis for formulating mitigation policies that balance mobility needs and environmental preservation. The results of the calculation of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the transportation sector show that total carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂ eq) emissions reached 61,384,220.81 CO₂ eq, with the largest contribution coming from CO₂ gas amounting to 59,966,119.65 CO₂ eq.

col5_Comment:
The total GHG emissions from the Energy sector of the province in 2022 amounted to 2,931.37 thousand tons of CO₂ equivalent. Among these, the manufacturing and construction industry (1A2) contributed the largest share, with approximately 2,175.65 thousand tons of CO₂e, accounting for 74.22% of the total emissions.
The transport sector (1A3) ranked second, contributing about 385 thousand tons of CO₂e, or 13.13%.
Emissions from other sub-sectors (1A4) — including commerce, services, and buildings (1A4a), residential (1A4b), and agriculture, forestry, and fisheries (1A4c) — totaled 370.72 thousand tons of CO₂e, representing 12.65%.
Within category 1A, the order of GHG emissions from highest to lowest is as follows:
manufacturing and construction (1A2), transport (1A3), and other sectors (1A4).

question_text: Provide a breakdown of your community-wide emissions by sector.
col5_Comment:
GHG emissions in the Industrial Processes and Product Use (IPPU) sector are calculated from industrial activities not related to the Energy sector.
The main emission sources in this sector arise from industrial production processes, specifically from the chemical or physical transformation of primary materials.

In 2022, GHG emissions from the IPPU sector of Quang Binh Province were estimated based on existing industrial processes, including cement production, lime production, metal (iron and steel) production, and product uses that substitute ozone-depleting substances (ODS).

According to the 2022 GHG inventory for each sub-sector within IPPU, the total GHG emissions from this sector amounted to 1,700.88 thousand tons of CO₂ equivalent.
Among them, cement production was by far the largest source, contributing 1,695.86 thousand tons of CO₂e (99.7%), followed by ceramic and brick production (0.27%), and the lowest emissions came from lime production (0.03%).

col1_Sector: Agriculture, Forestry and other land use (AFOLU)
col5_Comment:
The total GHG removals from the AFOLU sector of Quang Binh Province in 2022 amounted to 2,137.05 thousand tons of CO₂ equivalent. Specifically:

Emissions from Livestock (Category 3A): 301.45 thousand tons of CO₂e;

Removals from Land (Category 3B): 2,922.96 thousand tons of CO₂e;

Emissions from Other Sources and Non-CO₂ Emissions (Category 3C): 484.46 thousand tons of CO₂e.

Within Livestock (3A): emissions from enteric fermentation (3A1) were three times higher than those from manure management (3A2).

Within Land (3B): emissions were recorded from settlements (3B5) and other lands (3B6); meanwhile, forest land (3B1) represented the largest carbon sink, followed by cropland (3B2).

Within Other Sources and Non-CO₂ Emissions (3C): the largest emissions came from rice cultivation (3C7), followed by significant contributions from direct N₂O emissions from soils (3C4), then indirect N₂O emissions from soils (3C5), urea fertilization (3C3), biomass burning (3C1), indirect N₂O emissions from waste management (3C6), and finally liming (3C2).

question_text: Provide a breakdown of your community-wide emissions by sector.
col5_Comment:
The total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the Waste sector in Quang Binh Province in 2022 were estimated at 189.80 thousand tons of CO₂ equivalent.

Among the sub-sectors, solid waste disposal sites accounted for the largest share, with estimated emissions of 116.63 thousand tons of CO₂e, representing 61.45% of the total sectoral emissions.
The domestic wastewater treatment and discharge sub-sector ranked second, with 61.54 thousand tons of CO₂e, equivalent to 32.42% of the total.

The third-largest contributor was open burning of waste (4C2), responsible for 5.35% of total emissions from the Waste sector.
Two sub-sectors — industrial wastewater treatment and discharge (4D2) and waste incineration (4C1) — had the lowest emission levels among those with measurable emissions.
Other sub-sectors contributed negligible amounts compared to the total waste-related emissions in Quang Binh Province.

col5_Comment: The transport sector is the dominant contributor to Balanga's GHG emissions. This reflects the city's growing urbanization, reliance on private and public vehicles, and the increasing demand for mobility associated with economic activity. Road congestion and dependence on fossil-fuel powered vehicles amplify emissions.\n\nThis heavy share indicates the need for transport demand management, modernization of public transport fleets, promotion of non-motorized mobility (walking, cycling), and the introduction of electric vehicles or alternative fuels. Without intervention, emissions will continue to rise as urban population and vehicle ownership increase.
